category_l2: Unbounded allocation: the ClientHello handshake length (attacker-controlled 24-bit field) is used directly as ByteBuf capacity before the bytes arrive, so a short crafted record costs up to 16MB of heap per connection

fix_commits.message: Merge pull request from GHSA-6mjq-h674-j845

fixed_releases.verified_content: At 4.1.94.Final SslClientHelloHandler has MAX_CLIENT_HELLO_LENGTH=0xFFFFFF, a maxClientHelloLength field and constructors, and rejects handshakeLength > maxClientHelloLength with TooLongFrameException before allocating; SniHandler and AbstractSniHandler expose the limit through new constructors. The guard requires maxClientHelloLength != 0, and most default paths pass 0: AbstractSniHandler() calls this(0, 0L), SniHandler(Mapping) -> SniHandler(AsyncMapping) -> this(mapping, 0, 0L), and the handshake-timeout-only constructors delegate with 0 as well. The no-argument SslClientHelloHandler defaults to 0xFFFFFF, which getUnsignedMedium can never exceed. The mitigation therefore only takes effect when the application explicitly passes a maxClientHelloLength in [1, 0xFFFFFF].

category_l2: Encoded path separator (%2F/%2f/%5C/%5c) routing/decoding mismatch: the router matches the raw encoded path, while StaticDirectoryHandler and middleware.Static unescape before resolving files, so a request can evade route/group middleware and read a file under the configured static root. The first fix (4.15.3/5.2.0) rejected only encoded separators and was partial; 4.15.4/5.2.1 disable static path unescaping by default.

The global mirrors have NOT caught up: api.github.com/advisories and the advisory-database JSON are still updated_at/modified 2026-08-25T16:13:29Z with '< 4.15.3' / '< 5.2.0'; OSV GHSA (modified 2026-09-10), GO-2026-6293 (2026-08-26), the CVE CNA and NVD (2026-06-26) all still name 4.15.3/5.2.0. discrepancies.detail: The first fix rejected only encoded separators (%2F/%2f/%5C/%5c). Other percent-encoded paths still reached the unescape, so /%61dmin/secret.txt and /public/%2E%2E/admin/secret.txt still returned the protected file at v4.15.3 (reproduced: 200 + TOP-SECRET, go test exit=1) and at v4.15.4 they return 404 (exit=0). The complete fix (v4.15.4 / d16a4ecf, v5.2.1 / 78c3d95) removes internal/pathutil and makes Static/StaticFS and the Static middleware stop unescaping by default; unescaping is opt-in through Echo.EnablePathUnescapingStaticFiles / StaticConfig.EnablePathUnescaping. The v4.15.4 CHANGELOG calls this a breaking change. The v4.15.4 middleware test keeps an explicit 'nok, encoded slash bypasses ACL when EnablePathUnescaping=true' case, so the opted-in configuration remains vulnerable by design.

category_l2: Reverse-proxy response handling: finalizeResponse returns early for HTTP 101 Switching Protocols before removeConnectionHeaders and the hopHeaders deletion loop, and handleUpgradeResponse copies the whole upstream header map, so hop-by-hop headers (Alt-Svc, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Authenticate, Transfer-Encoding, Trailer, Connection-named headers) reach the client on WebSocket upgrades while being stripped on ordinary responses.

The red/green run shows the two 101 tests fail at v2.11.4 and pass at v2.11.5, and the end-to-end harness shows the three leaked headers disappearing.

severity.derivation_method: CVSS 3.1 base metrics were chosen by the collector from the verified code path and the advisory text, then the base score was computed with the official 3.1 formula: AV:N (a remote client receives the upstream's response), AC:H (the upstream must be malicious or compromised and must answer the upgrade), PR:N, UI:R (the client must open the WebSocket upgrade), S:U, C:N (the leaked headers give no direct read of protected data), I:L (injected hop-by-hop headers can alter client/proxy connection state), A:N. The independent reviewer must recompute this vector and may replace or reject it; if the reviewer rejects it, the dossier must not be promoted.
severity.discrepancy_note: Severity is the only field in this dossier that is not a published value. Every published CVSS slot is null; the advisory provides only the label 'low'. The score is a documented analyst reading, flagged so that it can be audited and replaced.

metric_rationale.A: N - the repro shows no availability impact.
metric_rationale.AC: H - exploitation presupposes a malicious or compromised upstream that sets the headers; the client cannot inject them through Caddy.
metric_rationale.AV: N - the 101 response is delivered over the network to any client that opens the proxied WebSocket route.
metric_rationale.C: N - the repro shows header leakage only; no protected data is read.
metric_rationale.I: L - Alt-Svc/Set-Cookie/Proxy-Authenticate injection can change client connection state, but no integrity compromise was demonstrated beyond that.
metric_rationale.PR: N - no privileges on Caddy or the upstream are required of the victim.
metric_rationale.S: U - the impact stays within the client/proxy connection.
metric_rationale.UI: R - the victim has to establish the upgraded connection for the leaked response headers to reach it.

severity.numeric_level_rationale: The derived base score is 3.1, which is Low (0.1-3.9) and agrees with the advisory's published qualitative label 'low'. Because no published numeric metric exists, this score must not be cited as a vendor or CNA score.
severity.source: Analyst-derived CVSS 3.1 base metric; NOT vendor-published. The repository advisory publishes severity=low but leaves cvss.score/vector_string and both cvss_severities entries null, and no other database (global GHSA, OSV, NVD, CVE.org) has a record for CVE-2026-55458.

category_l2: Code injection through template compilation: `_.template` merges the caller-supplied `options.imports` with `assignInWith` (so inherited enumerable keys are copied), never validates the merged key names, and passes them as parameter names to `Function(importsKeys, ...)`. Key names containing commas, parentheses, braces, brackets, slashes or whitespace break out of the parameter list and execute at template call time. Only the separate `variable` option was validated, a gap left by the CVE-2021-23337 fix.
discrepancies: Patched-version disagreement: CVE.org and the GitHub advisory say 4.18.1; OSV and NVD's CPE range say 4.18.0. Source inspection shows the validation already present in 4.18.0. The dossier records 4.18.1 and states the 4.18.0 caveat.

The advisory's only fix reference, 3469357c (2021-02-17), is the CVE-2021-23337 `variable`-option fix and is an ancestor of 4.17.21, 4.17.23, 4.18.0 and 4.18.1. A check that treats any referenced fix commit as an ancestor as 'not affected' would wrongly clear this snapshot. The real fix, 879aaa93, is identified by its message (it names both this CVE and the GHSA), its diff, and its ancestry: absent at 4.17.23, present at 4.18.0/4.18.1.
Severity disagreement: NVD primary 9.8 CRITICAL (AC:L) versus CNA/GitHub/OSV 8.1 HIGH (AC:H). Same impact metrics, different attack complexity.

lodash 4.17.22 was never published to npm (registry time and versions jump 4.17.21 to 4.17.23), yet every advisory range includes it. Ranges over this ecosystem must not be read as 'every version in between exists'.

The published npm tarball of 4.17.23 ships a lodash.js (sha256 71b4b7f5) that differs from the git tag blob (sha256 2dc5f1b8) yet contains the same vulnerable construct at the same lines and reproduces. The snapshot is the git tag; the npm build is independent corroboration, not the snapshot content.

The plain release tag 4.17.23 and the channel tag 4.17.23-npm are different commits (dec55b7a, 159 files vs 835a537f, 1054 built files). The evaluation target is the plain source tag; the channel tag was considered and rejected as a distribution artifact (see the abandoned 4.17.22-npm recon).

npm marks lodash@4.18.0 deprecated with the message 'Bad release. Please use lodash@4.17.21 instead.' (lodash-es, lodash-amd and lodash.template 4.18.0 are likewise deprecated). That explains why CVE.org and the GitHub advisory recommend 4.18.1 while OSV and NVD's CPE boundary stop at 4.18.0. The reason for the deprecation is not documented in the repository history; only the npm deprecation string is public evidence.

The published lower bound >=4.0.0 is incomplete: the same imports-key injection reproduces on lodash 3.10.1, which has the assignWith/Function sink at 10727/10810 and no reForbiddenIdentifierChars check (see affected_packages[0].range_completeness). The upper bound is unaffected. The dataset keeps the authoritative published range instead of inventing a wider one, and does not claim to know the lowest affected version.

The absence of 4.17.22 is specific to the lodash package: lodash-es published 4.17.22 on 2025-12-16 and lodash-amd on 2025-12-17, and the repository carries 4.17.22-amd/-es/-npm channel tags, but there is no plain 4.17.22 tag. Every advisory range includes a version that does not exist for the package this snapshot tracks.

At 4.18.1 the inherited-key variant does not throw: the fix also replaced assignInWith with assignWith, so an imports key inherited through the prototype is dropped before validation. Only own-key variants raise 'Invalid `imports` option passed into `_.template`'. Nothing executes in either case, so the fix is complete for both shapes.

The published npm tarball's package/package.json has no `private` field (npm strips it) while the git tag's package.json sets private: true. Artifact metadata is not byte-identical to the tag; the tarball's lodash.js differs from the tag blob only in two jsdoc comment lines (20-line unified diff, no code change).

GitHub publishes two different first-patched versions for the same advisory: the rendered repository advisory page says 4.18.1 (quoted in range_expressions), while the GitHub Advisory Database JSON read through the API during the independent selection review of 2026-10-22 says 4.18.0. This is a GitHub-internal inconsistency, not a transcription error, and it does not affect the snapshot's affected status.

Publication timestamps differ by surface: the rendered repository advisory page says 2026-03-31T19:03:35Z (recorded in published_at), CVE.org says 2026-03-31T19:25:55.987Z (recorded in published_at_cve_org), and OSV says 2026-04-01T23:51:12Z. All three are kept; none is a substitute for another.

Validating every key against the same regex used for the variable option, and no longer copying inherited properties through assignWith, closes both the direct and the prototype-polluted key variants; the red/green run confirms execution at 4.17.23 and refusal at 4.18.1.

NVD CPE configuration, lastModified 2026-06-17
Debian OSV DEBIAN-CVE-2019-6285, Debian 12/13/14

category_l2: Uncontrolled recursion in the single-document YAML parser: SingleDocParser::HandleFlowSequence consumes a '[' token, calls HandleNode, and HandleNode dispatches back into HandleFlowSequence for the next '['. There is no depth counter anywhere in the parser at 0.6.2, so a document of n opening brackets creates O(n) nested C++ stack frames and the process crashes with SIGSEGV before any syntax error is reported. The same cycle exists for flow maps ('{'), compact maps and the scanner's token queue; the 0.7.0 fix bounds it with a DepthGuard at HandleNode.
discrepancies: Fixed-version disagreement between ecosystems: Debian's tracker and OSV record say fixed_version 0.6.3-1, while upstream vanilla 0.6.3 still crashes and the fix commit 4edff1f is not an ancestor of 0.6.3. Debian 0.6.3-1 is a patched package that backports PR 807 (its changelog names CVE-2019-6285 and the patch says it 'cherry-picks the (so-far-unmerged) upstream pull request'). The first upstream release containing the fix is 0.7.0, and that is what the dossier records as the fixed release.

Two sibling CVEs (CVE-2018-20573 Scanner::EnsureTokensInQueue, CVE-2018-20574 HandleFlowMap) are labelled CWE-119 by NVD while CVE-2019-6285 and CVE-2019-6292 are labelled CWE-674. All four are the same stack-exhaustion defect fixed by the same commit; CWE-119 is a misclassification of uncontrolled recursion as a buffer issue.

The CVE.org CNA container ships a placeholder affected object: vendor, product and version are all 'n/a' and problemTypes is 'n/a', so the record itself states no version, CVSS or CWE. Its only reference is issue 660; the CVE Program ADP container adds a 2024 seclists fulldisclosure post. The exact 0.6.2 range comes from NVD's CPE and OSV's GIT range, not from the CVE record itself.

The affected range is not exhaustive: vanilla 0.6.3 is also affected although the published Debian range ends at 0.6.3-1, and older releases with the same parser (0.6.0, 0.6.1, and 0.5.x for the 2017 CVE) were not bisected. The published range and CPE name only 0.6.2.

The fix merged upstream with DepthGuard<2000> but the 0.7.0 release carries DepthGuard<500>, lowered by commit c2793a3 (2020-07-23, 'Fix runtime exceptions in Visual Studio environment. (#926)'). The recorded fixed release therefore rejects nesting at depth 500, not 2000.

CVE-2019-6292 is not covered by a named regression test in the fix commit, although it shares the same root cause and issue family (issue 657 lists HandleCompactMap, HandleMap, HandleFlowSequence, HandleSequence and HandleNode). The fix is family-wide because every path goes through HandleNode.
Publication timestamps differ by surface: CVE.org says 2019-01-14T22:00:00Z, NVD and OSV say 2019-01-14T22:29:00.390Z. Both are kept; neither replaces the other.

GHSA-hg7f-3vww-rc69 publishes the CVE as an identifier, but that advisory is not mirrored into OSV (api.osv.dev returns 404 for the GHSA id), so OSV's alias list for CVE-2019-6285 is empty. The GHSA edge is recorded from the GitHub advisory API instead. No source publishes an upstream semver range: only NVD's CPE, OSV's GIT range and Debian's downstream ECOSYSTEM range name versions.
NVD status is Modified, not final, and the record was last modified 2026-06-17; the score and CPE may still change.

fix_commits.content: Adds include/yaml-cpp/depthguard.h (DeepRecursion exception and a DepthGuard<max_depth=2000> RAII counter), src/depthguard.cpp, an int depth member on SingleDocParser, DepthGuard<2000> at the top of HandleNode, and four regression tests named CVE_2017_5950, CVE_2018_20573, CVE_2018_20574 and CVE_2019_6285. A later commit (c2793a3, 'Fix runtime exceptions in Visual Studio environment. (#926)') lowered the HandleNode guard to 500 before the 0.7.0 release.
fix_commits.message: Fix stack overflow (#807)
fix_commits.why_complete: The recursion cycle is HandleNode -> HandleFlowSequence -> HandleNode, and every entrance to it passes through HandleNode, so one counter at HandleNode's entry bounds all SingleDocParser recursion shapes (flow sequences, flow maps, compact maps and block collections). The independent red/green run shows SIGSEGV at 0.6.2 and DeepRecursion at 0.7.0 for the same inputs.

category_l2: Uncaught error in the microservice server: ServerTCP#handleMessage and ServerRMQ#handleMessage convert a client-controlled non-string message pattern with JSON.stringify to derive the handler lookup key. JSON.parse accepts nesting that JSON.stringify cannot re-serialise, so a deeply nested pattern parses on arrival and then throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. The listener's promise is not caught, the RangeError becomes an unhandled rejection, and Node.js exits under its default --unhandled-rejections=throw. The fix guards the stringification with getPatternAsString and routes handleMessage rejections to handleError.
discrepancies: The fix references do not agree with release containment. GHSA, OSV, NVD and CVE.org all name aa97b514 (the PR head) as a fix commit, but that commit is an ancestor of no tag; the PR was squash-merged as e93c8e12b (in v12.0.2+) and the 11.x line received the dedicated backport e9dcd4c7 (in v11.2.4+). The dossier records all three with their measured ancestry so no reader mistakes aa97b514 for the release-bearing fix.

The publication timestamps differ by surface: CVE.org and OSV say 2026-09-28T21:21:25Z, NVD says 2026-09-28T22:17:32Z, and the GHSA API says 2026-09-29T23:54:44Z. The catalog candidate record says 2026-09-15T08:38:29Z, which is earlier than every advisory surface; the row uses NVD's timestamp and keeps the others here.

NVD's status is 'Awaiting Analysis', not 'Analyzed'. Its only CVSS metric is the GitHub CNA Secondary 3.1 7.5; there is no NVD primary metric and no NVD CPE configuration. The CPE-style range comes from NVD's 'affected' block, which is the CNA's data, not an NVD analysis.

The GHSA says the patched versions are 12.0.2 and 11.2.4 but recommends upgrading to 12.0.3 / 11.2.5. Both 11.2.4 and 12.0.2 are inside the range of the separate advisory GHSA-96h4-vgxj-gvm2, fixed in 11.2.5 / 12.0.3. The row keeps 11.2.4 and 12.0.2 as this CVE's fixed releases because those are the first releases containing this fix.

Two CWEs are assigned. CWE-248 (Uncaught Exception) names the mechanism that terminates the process; CWE-674 (Uncontrolled Recursion) names the stringify recursion. Both are recorded; neither replaces the other.

OSV's GIT range places the 11.x fix at the v11.2.4 tag commit d5046225 and the 12.x fix at the v12.0.2 tag commit ee168a56, while the advisory-level fixed commits are the code commits e9dcd4c7 / e93c8e12b. The tag commits are release commits that contain the code fixes; the ancestry checks were run for both the code commits and the tags.

The microservices package version and the monorepo root version differ: at v11.2.3 packages/microservices/package.json is 11.2.3 while the root package.json is 11.1.26. The affected package is the npm package, not the root monorepo version.

Only the TCP and RabbitMQ transports are affected. The collector reproduced the TCP path only; the RMQ path is asserted from the identical unguarded call at server-rmq.ts 300-302 and the backport diff, not from a broker run. Other transports take the pattern as a string from the broker and never stringify a client object.

Message says 'Backport of aa97b5144d (master)'. 6 files, +107/-18.

category_l2: JoinHandle::abort() performs the task shutdown on the calling thread. For a task spawned on a LocalSet the future must only ever be dropped on the LocalSet's thread, so aborting from another thread moves arbitrary !Send state, such as Rc or RefCell contents, across threads. category_l2: The GIF LZW decoder pushes decoded indices onto a fixed 4096-entry stack without bounding the stack pointer. A crafted code stream makes the prefix-chain walk keep pushing, so the writes run past the end of the stack and the process aborts; a malformed GIF therefore crashes a decoder that loads untrusted images.

category_l2: Plug.Cowboy.Conn.conn/1 calls String.to_atom/1 on :cowboy_req.scheme(req). For HTTP/2 the ':scheme' pseudo-header is client-controlled and passed through verbatim, so each unique scheme value interns a new BEAM atom that is never reclaimed; an unauthenticated client can exhaust the 1,048,576-entry atom table and abort the VM with system_limit. v2.8.1 maps only "http"/"https" and raises CaseClauseError otherwise.

It is referenced as the fix by the GHSA/EEF/CVE records and NVD, and is an ancestor of v2.8.1 and absent from v2.8.0. The CVE record additionally lists the v2.8.1 release commit fd0841f4 as a fixed event.

category_l2: Ecto.Repo.Queryable.query_for_get_by/3 special-cases {key, nil} into is_nil(field(x, ^key)) instead of letting the query builder reject a comparison with nil. category_l2: artifactV4Routes.buildSignature feeds endpoint, expires, artifactName, taskID and artifactID into the HMAC as raw concatenated bytes. Because artifactName has no delimiter or length prefix before the decimal taskID/artifactID, distinct tuples can serialize to the same byte stream (e.g. artifactName 'artifact-795-153' with taskID 48 versus artifactName 'artifact-795-1' with taskID 53, artifactID '48<id>'): the signature verifies for a tuple the signer never approved. The UploadArtifact and DownloadArtifact routes are unauthenticated and guarded only by ArtifactV4Contexter; after verification verifySignature loads the task by the URL's taskID and the handlers look the artifact up by name, so a forged tuple can read another task's/repository's artifact or write into another task's upload staging state.

fix_commits.note: 1c2d5e9b is the release-branch backport of PR #37707 (#37795). It replaces the concatenation with actions.BuildSignature, which length-prefixes string fields and encodes integers as fixed-width binary, and applies the same hardening to routers/api/v1/repo/action.go; ancestor of v1.26.2/v1.26.3/v1.26.4 only.

category_l2: Urlizer.trim_punctuation() trims wrapping punctuation in a fixpoint loop. For every candidate opening/closing pair it calls middle.count(closing) and middle.count(opening) on the whole word, and each iteration only removes one bracket per side, so a word made of tens of thousands of brackets is rescanned once per bracket. Because handle_word() calls trim_punctuation() for any word containing '.', '@' or ':', passing such text through the urlize/urlizetrunc template filters consumes quadratic CPU and memory (CWE-130 improper handling of length parameter inconsistency; CWE-770 allocation without limits).

category_l2: The floatformat template filter converts its input with Decimal(str(text)) and then computes `int(d) - d`. Decimal keeps a scientific-notation value as a short coefficient plus an exponent, so parsing is cheap, but int(d) materialises every digit implied by the exponent. A string such as '1e10000000000000000' therefore asks for an astronomically large integer and exhausts memory. The 4.2.15 fix inspects Decimal.as_tuple() first and returns the input unchanged when len(digits)+abs(exponent) > 200 (CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption).

fix_commits.note: '[4.2.x] Fixed CVE-2024-41989' reads Decimal.as_tuple() and returns the input as-is when len(digits)+abs(exponent) > 200, before int(d); adds the 1e199 boundary, huge-exponent and million-digit regression cases and the 4.2.15 release-note entry.
'[5.0.x] Fixed CVE-2024-41989' applies the same 200-digit cutoff on the 5.0 line.

category_l2: Urlizer.handle_word matches simple_url_re/simple_url_2_re against the whole untruncated word and, on a match, sends every character through smart_urlquote() (urlsplit, punycode on the netloc, unquote/quote on the path) with no length cap; is_email_simple() has no bound on the domain part, so a multi-megabyte unicode domain also reaches punycode(). AdminURLFieldWidget.get_context() calls smart_urlquote() on the raw value whenever the value is truthy, even when the validator already rejected it (url_valid False). At 4.2.13 a 1M-character unicode URL costs seconds in urlize() and a 4M-character value costs ~10 s and ~200 MB in the widget, which also builds an 18M-character href. The 4.2.15 fix caps URLs at MAX_URL_LENGTH = 2048, rejects domain parts longer than 63 characters, and quotes the widget href only when url_valid (CWE-1284 improper validation of specified quantity; CWE-1333 inefficient regular expression complexity).

category_l2: strip_tags() (django/utils/html.py) re-runs _strip_once() in a while loop until the number of '<' characters stops changing, with no bound on the number of iterations. _strip_once() feeds the whole remaining string to MLStripper(HTMLParser) and removes exactly one level of nesting per pass, so an input of the form '<'*d + 'a>'*d is scanned d times: O(d * len(value)). At 4.2.13 a 24,000-character input (d=8000) takes 25.78 s; depth 500 already costs 0.0996 s and each doubling of d multiplies the cost by about four. The striptags template filter exposes the same path to template content. 4.2.17 adds MAX_STRIP_TAGS_DEPTH = 50 and raises SuspiciousOperation once the loop reaches the cap, so the same inputs fail in 0.018-0.333 s (CWE-770 allocation of resources without limits or throttling).

category_l2: HasKeyLookup.as_oracle() (django/db/models/fields/json.py) composes the Oracle SQL in two steps: HasKeyLookup.as_sql() builds 'JSON_EXISTS(<lhs>, %s)' from the lhs SQL and returns the lhs bind params together with the JSON paths, and as_oracle() then applies `sql % tuple(params)` to that composed string and returns an empty param list. Every lhs parameter is therefore pasted into the SQL text instead of being sent as a bind variable, so when application code passes untrusted data as the lhs of a direct HasKey(lhs, rhs) query, that data becomes SQL syntax. At 4.2.13 an lhs of "'x') OR 1=1 --" compiles to JSON_EXISTS('x') OR 1=1 --, '$."a"') with no params; a JSON object lhs is inlined the same way. The 4.2.17 fix splits the composition into _as_sql_parts()/_combine_sql_parts() and gives as_oracle() a template that inlines only the JSON path while returning the lhs params, so the same lhs compiles to JSON_EXISTS(%s, '$."a"') with the value bound. The has_key lookup through __ is unaffected on both releases (CWE-89).

category_l2: Truncator._truncate_html (django/utils/text.py 215-300 at 4.2.13) walks the input with re_chars/re_words and keeps the open tags in a plain list. For every end tag it calls `open_tags.index(tagname)` (line 276) and, on a hit, rebuilds the list with `open_tags = open_tags[i + 1 :]` (line 282). An input made of start tags followed by many unmatched end tags never hits that branch, so each of the m end tags scans all m open tags and the parse costs O(m^2) Python-level comparisons - about 3.1 s for 112 KB (n=16,000) in the measured ladder, with a ~1.9 log2 slope per doubling. Because the payload contains no text characters, `current_len` never reaches `truncate_len`, so the loop keeps parsing every tag even when the caller asks for a tiny preview (truncatechars_html:2, truncatewords_html:1). 4.2.28 replaces the scan with the LIFO check `if open_tags and open_tags[0] == tagname` and the list slice with `open_tags[1:]`, which removes the Python-level scan; the `open_tags.insert(0, tagname)` call and the per-close slice copy remain, so the backport is ~10-21x faster on this payload but is not linear on well-nested input either.

category_l2: In django/http/multipartparser.py, the base64 branch of the file part loop strips whitespace from the current parser chunk (stripped_chunk, 305), then aligns it to a multiple of four by calling `field_stream.read(4 - remaining)` (309) once per 1-3 bytes and appending in place (312). category_l2: UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response() skips caching a response that sets a cookie and varies on Cookie only when the incoming request carried no cookies at all (the `not request.COOKIES` precondition, 91-98). A request that already carries any unrelated cookie - a language or theme preference, a consent flag - therefore stores the response, including its newly issued session cookie and private body, in the shared cache under a key that varies only by the Cookie header. cache_page() wraps the same CacheMiddleware through decorator_from_middleware_with_args(), so the decorator inherits the defect. 5.2.16 drops the precondition and refuses to cache whenever response.cookies and has_vary_header(response, "Cookie") hold.

category_l2: UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response() calls django.utils.cache.has_vary_header() to decide whether a response may be cached: the Cookie guard refuses to cache a cookie-less request's response that sets a cookie, and (since 5.0) the wildcard guard refuses Vary: *. has_vary_header() splits the Vary value on commas and lowercases the parts without stripping surrounding whitespace, so Vary: ' Cookie' or ' *' is not recognized. The response is stored under a key that also ignores the spaced header name, and FetchFromCacheMiddleware serves it to other clients. The upstream fix adds .strip(); 4.2 LTS was end-of-life and has no patched release, and its middleware has no wildcard guard at all, so the 4.2 exposure that the fix would remove is the Cookie-guard bypass.

category_l2: QuerySet.annotate()/alias() register a dictionary-expanded alias after check_alias(), which at 4.2.13 rejects quotes, whitespace, semicolons and SQL comments but not periods. When the same alias is used in FilteredRelation and then in order_by(), SQLCompiler.get_order_by() sees the period, assumes the entry came from extra(order_by=...), splits it as table.column and emits that verbatim as RawSQL in ORDER BY. The annotation lookup is bypassed, so a crafted alias chooses the table and column used for ordering. The 4.2.28 fix restricts the dotted branch to extra_order_by entries and makes add_filtered_relation() reject periods in aliases.

category_l2: Query aliases are validated by Query.check_alias() against FORBIDDEN_ALIAS_PATTERN. At 4.2.13 the pattern rejects quotes, whitespace, semicolons, hashes absent and SQL comments, but not the control-character ranges 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F-0x9F. Those keys can reach annotate(), alias(), aggregate(), extra(), values() and values_list() through dictionary expansion, are stored as column aliases and are emitted inside the SQL identifier. The 4.2.28 fix adds both control-character ranges to the pattern and updates the ValueError message; the tests sweep every code point in those ranges for annotate(), alias() and FilteredRelation.

category_l2: QuerySet.alias()/annotate() route a FilteredRelation alias supplied through **kwargs dictionary expansion to Query.add_filtered_relation(), which stores the attacker-chosen key as the join alias. category_l2: HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__ sets the Location header and then calls urlparse(str(redirect_to)) so the destination scheme can be checked. At 4.2.13 there is no upper bound on that string: a very large attacker-supplied redirect target reaches urllib.parse.urlsplit(), which NFKC-normalizes a non-ASCII netloc with unicodedata.normalize(). Python's NFKC normalization is slow on Windows, so repeated large redirects can exhaust CPU. The same path is reachable through HttpResponsePermanentRedirect and django.shortcuts.redirect(). 4.2.26 adds a 2048-character cap before urlparse, relaxed to 16384 in 4.2.27.

category_l2: GeoDjango hands WKT/WKB/hex-WKB straight to GEOS. Before GEOS 3.15.0 the WKT/WKB readers recurse once per nested GEOMETRYCOLLECTION with no depth cap, so deeply nested input overflows the stack and segfaults the process. category_l2: The Content-Disposition header regex is not anchored to the start of a line and pairs a greedy (.*) with an end-of-line lookahead, so the regexp engine restarts the scan at every offset where the literal occurs. The 1536-byte disposition cap is applied after the match and the header block is bounded only by the blank-line terminator. When one part header line contains many literal occurrences and no CRLF followed by a non-whitespace character after them (a folded continuation line starting with whitespace is enough), every occurrence pays an O(rest of line) backtracking scan, i.e. quadratic work in the header-line length. A single occurrence followed by a long value only pays one scan and stays linear. v3.1.16 anchors all three header regexes at ^ with FWS/HEADER_VALUE.

category_l2: handle_mime_head waits for the CRLFCRLF that terminates a MIME part header by scanning the shared buffer with @head_regex. When the terminator has not arrived, the buffer is appended to (read_data: io.read(@bufsize) then @sbuf.concat) and the loop returns :want_read with no cap on how many bytes may accumulate, so a part header that never terminates is buffered in memory up to the request body size. There is no amplification: memory grows with the bytes actually sent, so the bound is the server's body limit and concurrency. v3.1.17 raises 'multipart mime part header too large' once the buffer exceeds MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT = 64 KiB (effectively max(64 KiB, BUFSIZE)).

category_l2: handle_fast_forward looks for the first multipart boundary by scanning the shared buffer with consume_boundary (@sbuf.scan_until(@body_regex)). When the boundary has not arrived the else branch only returns :want_read, and read_data (io.read(@bufsize) then @sbuf.concat) keeps appending, so every byte sent before the first boundary stays resident in memory. consume_boundary calls @sbuf.terminate on failure, which moves the scan pointer to the end but does not free the string. There is no amplification in retained bytes: the resident string grows with the bytes actually sent, so the bound is the server's body limit plus concurrency (peak RSS can still reach about 1.6-2x the payload because Ruby String growth copies the buffer; the round39 reviewer measured VmHWM 141,404 kB against a 25,856 kB baseline for a 64 MiB preamble). v3.1.17 raises 'multipart boundary not found within limit' once the whole buffer is larger than BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT = 16 KiB; the check runs after each read, so the first threshold hit is the first BUFSIZE multiple above 16 KiB (1,048,576 B by default, 24,576 B with BUFSIZE 8192).

fix_commits.note: 'Fix denial of service vulnerbilties in multipart parsing' (subject spelling as upstream): adds BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT and the boundary raise for this CVE, and MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT for the sibling CVE-2025-61772. category_l2: Parts without a filename take the BufferPart branch: Collector#on_mime_head allocates body = String.new (parser.rb 160) and Collector#on_mime_body appends every chunk with @mime_parts[mime_index].body << content (170). Nothing counts the retained bytes: check_part_limits (178-195) bounds only the number of open files and the number of parts, and handle_mime_body hands over the entire part body once the boundary is found (414) or the growing tail on each read (422). A single large text field is therefore materialised in process memory. There is no amplification: retained memory tracks the bytes the client actually sends, so the bound is the server's body limit plus concurrency. v3.1.17 accounts header bytes plus non-file body bytes and raises 'multipart data over retained size limit' once @retained_size exceeds BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (default 16 MiB, configurable through RACK_MULTIPART_BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT).

category_l2: Rack::Request#POST parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies by calling get_header(RACK_INPUT).read with no length argument (request.rb 531 at v3.1.13), which is IO#read(nil): read everything until EOF into one Ruby String, before any size check runs. The frozen QueryParser at this tag has no byte or count limits at all (query_parser.rb 30-39: initialize takes only params_class and param_depth_limit, and the file has no BYTESIZE_LIMIT / PARAMS_LIMIT / QueryLimitError), so neither the read nor the subsequent parse is bounded. Memory therefore tracks the request body size linearly, with no amplification. 3.1.18 reads at most query_parser.bytesize_limit + 2 bytes (4 MiB default via RACK_QUERY_PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT) and falls back to '' when read returns nil.

The frozen request.rb at that commit has the unbounded read at 531 and its query_parser.rb has no size limit at all; the fix commits cbd541e8 / e179614c / 4e2c9039 are not ancestors of v3.1.13 (git_ancestry.txt). category_l2: Rack::Sendfile decides whether to enable sendfile, and which redirect header to emit, from request headers rather than from configuration. At v3.1.13 variation() (sendfile.rb 148-152) falls back to env['HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE'] when the middleware was constructed without a variation, so a client can turn on x-accel-redirect (or x-sendfile, which reflects the absolute path of a to_path body). When the x-accel-redirect branch runs, map_accel_path() (154-165) falls back to env['HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING'] (157) whenever no application-level mapping matched, so the client controls the filesystem-to-URL substitution that ends up in the response header at 123. A proxy that re-issues x-accel-redirect internally then serves the mapped private location unless it overwrites both headers, which is why the advisory requires the proxy to always set or strip them. Fixed in 3.1.18 by removing the HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE fallback entirely, gating HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING behind explicit x-accel-redirect configuration with no app mappings, and anchoring the mapping regexes with \A instead of ^.

fix_commits.note: 'Improper handling of proxy headers in Rack::Sendfile may allow proxy bypass.': drops the HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE fallback (variation is now @variation || env['sendfile.type']), adds x_accel_mapping() which returns the header only when x-accel-redirect is configured explicitly and no app mappings exist, and replaces ^ with \A in both mapping regexes. category_l2: Flask adds Vary: Cookie so shared caches key on the session cookie. At 2.3.1 the flag that gates the header (SecureCookieSession.accessed) is set only in __getitem__, get, setdefault and on_update (sessions.py 71-87); plain dict operations inherited from CallbackDict such as `key in session`, len(session) and iteration never set it, and flask.session / the template `session` both resolve to the same object, so those reads are invisible. In addition, at this tag save_session returns early on an empty session (334) before the Vary gate (347-349), so even a value read on an empty session yields no Vary. A caching proxy that does not ignore Set-Cookie responses can then serve a session-dependent response to another user. The fix moves tracking to RequestContext.session (3.1.3 ctx.py 368-375), so resolving the proxy sets accessed before any dict operation, drops the per-method overrides, stops replacing the proxy in the template context, and uses ctx._session when saving so the save itself does not count as access.

category_l2: Request.max_form_memory_size is meant to cap in-memory form data, and MultiPartParser.parse forwards it to MultipartDecoder. At 3.0.2 the only enforcement is in MultipartDecoder.receive_data (sansio/multipart.py 139-143), which compares len(buffer) + len(chunk) against the limit for a single chunk. MultiPartParser.parse reads the body in buffer_size (64 KiB) chunks (369) and, for a non-file field, appends every Data event to a list (381-382) with no cumulative accounting, then joins and decodes the whole list when the part ends (384-388). A body whose non-file field is larger than the limit but arrives in chunks smaller than it therefore passes every per-event check and is buffered without bound; a bigger buffer_size makes the same bypass trivial. The fix 50cfeebc/8760275a tracks field_size per Field (355, 374, 383-389) and raises RequestEntityTooLarge once the accumulated field passes the limit, leaving file parts to the streaming container.

category_l2: String callable resolution in address validation. validateAddress($address, $patternselect = null) falls back to static::$validator, which defaults to the string 'php', and then returns $patternselect($address) whenever is_callable() accepts the selector (src/PHPMailer.php 1309-1311 at v6.1.5). A plain string is callable exactly when a function of that name exists in the global namespace, so a function that another primitive injected — even one unrelated to mail, named 'php' — is executed for every address validated in the default configuration, and its return value becomes the validation verdict. The fix 45f3c18d requires !is_string($patternselect) at 1341 of v6.5.0, so a string always reaches the built-in switch (case 'php' -> filter_var) and only closures/arrays are called.

title: Websites were able to send any requests to the vite development server and read the response
vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.0.11 peels to b44c4930 (git_facts), the commit the evaluation snapshot snap_2e50b228f2432623 pins; packages/vite/package.json in the built worktree reads version 5.0.11. The OSV SEMVER range 5.0.0 -> 5.4.12 contains 5.0.11, and NVD's CPE versionStartIncluding 5.0.0 / versionEndExcluding 5.4.12 does too.

category_l2: fetch() parses the integrity option with a regular expression that only recognises a hash token when at least one base64-ish character follows the algorithm. A value such as 'sha256-ä', 'sha256-!' or 'sha256-' does not parse, the parser skips it, and the resulting empty metadata set is accepted by the unchanged empty-set rule in bytesMatch. The body is then delivered even though no declared hash matched it. The fix keeps the algorithm token when the hash is absent so the comparison fails, which in practice closes the request through a TypeError. 5.28.4 fixes the 5.x line and 6.11.1 fixes the 6.x line; the two commits are separate backports with different patch-ids.

vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.19.0 is a lightweight tag on f5c89e5c (git_facts) and its package.json reports 5.19.0; the evaluation snapshot pins that commit. category_l2: The Request constructor's blob-like body branch appends `content-type: ${body.type}` to the request head without calling isValidHeaderValue. category_l2: The Request constructor accepts any string for the `upgrade` option and only checks its type. `lib/client.js` then appends `connection: upgrade\r\nupgrade: ${upgrade}\r\n` to the request head before the ordinary headers, so CR, LF or NUL bytes in the value terminate or extend the head. An attacker who influences that option can inject arbitrary request headers or smuggle a second request to the origin (the advisory points at non-HTTP services such as Redis, Memcached and Elasticsearch). Ordinary headers already go through `processHeaderValue` and its headerCharRegex in 5.x; the `upgrade` option is the one path that does not. The 6.24.0/7.24.0 fix reuses that same regex through `isValidHeaderValue` and throws `invalid upgrade header`. No 5.x release contains the fix.

category_l2: Weak randomness (CWE-330) in a security-relevant protocol field. `extractBody()` builds the multipart boundary as `----formdata-undici-${Math.random()}` (5.19.0) and as `----formdata-undici-0${floor(Math.random() * 1e11)}` (5.28.4), then reports it as the request's `content-type` parameter and in the body delimiters. Math.random is not a CSPRNG and its state is recovered from a handful of outputs, so an attacker who has observed previous multipart requests can predict the boundary of the next one and craft a body that the backend parses differently from the client (the advisory's stated impact). The fix routes the boundary through `crypto.randomInt(0, 1e11)` in 5.28.5 / 6.21.1 / 7.2.3.

category_l2: setCookie() serialises a cookie dictionary with stringify(): the domain is checked only for a leading '-', a trailing '.' or a trailing '-' (validateCookieDomain, lib/cookies/util.js 106-114), a path only for bytes below 0x21 and ';' (validateCookiePath, 91-99), and every unparsed entry is emitted as `${key}=${value}` after a bare '=' presence check (253-262). The fix validates the domain against the RFC 1034/1123 preferred name syntax, rejects path bytes above 0x7E, and runs unparsed keys/values through validateCookieName / validateCookieValue.

category_l2: The WebSocket receiver parses inbound frames in a loop (ByteParser.run). On a PING frame it consumes the payload, builds a PONG with WebsocketFrameSend and calls this.ws[kResponse].socket.write(frame.createFrame(opcodes.PONG)) (lib/websocket/receiver.js:148 at v5.19.0), then resets the state to INFO and continues while more buffered bytes remain. The value returned by socket.write() is discarded, and nothing consults socket.writableLength / writableNeedDrain, so when the peer never reads the PONGs each additional PING appends another frame to the outbound queue and the parser never yields. Because the PING payload is consumed as application data and the PONG carries it back, inbound bytes and retained outbound bytes are proportional; the vendor describes the attack as asymmetric, with availability the only impact. From 6.x the same write sits in parseControlFrame (line 483 at v6.29.0, line 486 at v7.30.0, line 496 at v8.12.1). The fixes (39f93e14 / 53944624 / b217373b) set #loop = false and register socket.once('drain', ...) when the reply leaves the socket over its high-water mark, bounding the queue.

category_l2: In httpNetworkFetch, the response's Content-Encoding header is split on ',' into codings (lib/fetch/index.js:1985-1986 at v5.19.0) and the loop at 2004-2015 pushes one zlib decompressor per coding into decoders, with no count limit; pipeline(this.body, ...decoders, () => {}) then chains every one of them (2018-2024). Nothing bounds the number of links, and because the header length is only limited by maxHeaderSize (16 KiB by default) a malicious server can list thousands of codings, so the client allocates thousands of streams and spends CPU and memory decompressing the same tiny body once per layer. From 6.x the same loop lives in lib/web/fetch/index.js; a separate decompress interceptor path (lib/interceptor/decompress.js, shipped from v7.15.0) builds the same unbounded chain. The fixes cap the chain at five: d3aafea7 / 4e9b88b1 reject fetch responses whose coding list is longer than five, and b04e3cbb applies the same ceiling in the interceptor.

category_l2: TLS certificate validation bypass (CWE-295): the Agent constructor stores `{ ...util.deepClone(options), connect }` (lib/agent.js:44-53), and deepClone is `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj))` (lib/core/util.js:146-148), so a caller-supplied `tls` object keeps only its JSON-representable fields. Client destructures `tls` and spreads it into buildConnector (lib/client.js:105, 186-192), which spreads it into tls.connect (lib/core/connect.js:96-100); the surviving ca/servername make default verification accept a peer the dropped checkServerIdentity would have rejected. `connect` is added after the clone, which is why the documented workaround works. The fix keeps tls outside the JSON clone.

title: undici Agent silently drops a function-valued tls.checkServerIdentity callback because it JSON-clones its constructor options, so a certificate the callback was written to reject passes Node's default chain/hostname checks
vulnerable_commit_basis: Tag v5.19.0 resolves to f5c89e5c and its package.json reports 5.19.0. lib/agent.js:51 stores `{ ...util.deepClone(options), connect }`, so a `tls.checkServerIdentity` passed to Agent is dropped before Client sees it (lib/client.js:105, 190). The collector probe over this worktree made a request to a certificate that its own callback rejects: the request succeeded with the callback never invoked, on 5.19.0 and on 5.28.5/5.29.0; the vendor regression test fails there with 'Missing expected rejection'. The advisory range '>= 4.0.0, < 6.29.1' contains 5.19.0, but the judgement rests on the executed bypass, not on the version string.

category_l2: On v5.19.0 the socket 'error' listener registered in lib/client.js (onSocketError, 923-939) opens with assert(err.code !== 'ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID') at line 926. During connect that error code is an expected, handled outcome — the connect-phase branch at 1124-1129 asserts client[kRunning] === 0 and fails the queued requests — so the assert encoded the belief that hostname verification cannot fail after a socket is established. TLS 1.2 renegotiation breaks that belief: Node re-runs checkServerIdentity on the renegotiated handshake, and a server that switches to a same-CA certificate for a different name makes the error arrive on the established socket, where the assert throws. Because it throws inside an EventEmitter listener there is no caller to catch it and the process aborts. Node's TLS stack does not enable renegotiation by default in every build and TLS 1.3 has no renegotiation, which is why the advisory scopes the bug to TLS 1.2. The same assert exists twice in the h2 paths (6.x client-h2.js 139 and 214; 7.x 296 and 439; 8.x 603 and 770) and once in the h1 path (6.x 730, 7.x 931, 8.x 991); b40fbfc0 / 12cfd96c / e257e9f8 delete all of them, leaving only the connect-phase special case.

category_l2: At v5.19.0 the h1 Parser (lib/client.js) accepts any response head the socket yields and attaches it to client[kQueue][client[kRunningIdx]]. onHeadersComplete (680-706) checks only that the socket is alive and that a queue slot exists; it never checks client[kRunning] === 0, i.e. that a request is actually in flight on this socket. After onMessageComplete (828-896) advances kRunningIdx and, for pipelining 1, defers dispatch with setImmediate, an application that issues its next request in that window can have the attacker's already-buffered bytes parsed as that request's response, because kPendingIdx has advanced and kRunningIdx now points at the pending request. The 6.27.0 / 7.28.0 / 8.5.0 fix adds exactly the missing in-flight test (util.destroy(socket, new SocketError('bad response')) when client[kRunning] === 0 in onStatus and onHeadersComplete), marks a socket that has carried a response with kSocketUsed, and makes resumeH1 validate an idle socket (kIdleSocketValidation with a 0 ms timer) before dispatching into it.

category_l2: Rack::Static#applicable_rules evaluates header rules against the PATH_INFO it is handed, which is still URL-encoded, while the file served is resolved from Utils.clean_path_info(Utils.unescape_path(PATH_INFO)); an encoded variant of a static path is therefore served without some of the headers the operator configured for that content class. The effect is order-dependent: a String rule earlier in the same header_rules list unescapes and reassigns path, so :fonts/Array/Regexp rules placed after it already see the decoded path.

category_l2: Rack::Directory builds each directory-index row with DIR_FILE, whose anchor is `<a href='%s'>`. The value substituted into href is the file's basename escaped with Rack::Utils.escape_path (which does not escape the ':' of a URI scheme) and then Rack::Utils.escape_html (which escapes quotes, '<' and '>' but does not neutralize a scheme). A file named `javascript:alert(1)` therefore produces href='javascript:alert(1)', which a browser resolves as a JavaScript URL in the listing's origin when a user clicks it

category_l2: Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges parses the HTTP Range header and builds one Range object per comma-separated spec with no upper bound on how many specs it will accept: byte_ranges delegates to get_byte_ranges, which splits $1 on /,\s*/ and loops over every element. The only rejection that depends on the set as a whole is the CVE-2024-26141 total-coverage check (`return [] if ranges.map(&:size).sum > size`), which a header built from many small overlapping specs such as `bytes=0-0,0-0,0-0,...` never trips. A ~200 KB header therefore allocates 200,000 Range objects before the response is even started, and Rack::Files then walks that array again to build a multipart/byteranges body, so one request buys disproportionate CPU, memory, I/O and bandwidth
